(b) He was the first speaker everywhere. Rashi, Menachot 103b, explains that he was called this because of the cave episode in tractate Shabbat [the received locator reads ד״מ ע״ד]. Heilprin suspects a scribal error and locates the story in Bameh Madlikin, Shabbat 33b, by the emperor's command: “Yehudah, who elevated, shall be elevated.” Tosafot in Menachot there says R. Yehudah was the instructor of Rabbi's household. Rashi, Menachot 104a, explains that he instructed Rabbi’s household in legal rulings. Tosafot says they acted by his instruction and suggests the emperor may have appointed him head over the patriarchal house. There, 104a, beginning, they write that R. Yehudah may have lived in his days, since even R. Meir, who died before R. Yehudah (see there), lived at R. Shimon son of Rabbi's wedding; see Rabbi above. Every story of an unqualified “pious man” concerns R. Yehudah ben Bava or R. Yehudah bar Ilai: Bava Kamma 103b, near the end. Temurah 15b, near the end: a pious man groaned from his heart. They consulted physicians, who said his only remedy was to suck hot milk each morning, etc. They examined him and found only that sin. There: every unqualified “pious man” is R. Yehudah ben Bava or R. Yehudah bar Ilai. Yet the Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 9:10:3 explicitly identifies this groaning man as R. Yehudah ben Bava; see there. Shabbat 127b: a pious man redeemed a girl, etc., and at the inn laid her beneath his feet. The next day he went down and immersed, then taught his students, etc. Rashi explains that every such “pious man” is R. Yehudah ben Bava or R. Yehudah bar Ilai. Why did Rashi not explain this in Berakhot, chapter 3, 18b, concerning the pious man and the two spirits conversing, or there, 32b, near the end, concerning the pious man praying who did not return an official's greeting? These too would be R. Yehudah ben Bava or R. Yehudah bar Ilai. The great teacher R. Heshel said: the difficulty is that we hold like R. Yehudah ben Beteira, who permits a man with a seminal emission to engage in Torah, Berakhot 22a. Why, then, did he need to immerse? Rashi therefore explains that this pious man is R. Yehudah bar Ilai, the unqualified R. Yehudah, who holds there that a man with a seminal emission may not engage in Torah. Birkat HaZevach, Temurah there, writes: Sanhedrin 20a says, “Grace is false”—Joseph, with Potiphar's wife; “beauty is vain”—Boaz, with Ruth; “a woman who fears the Lord shall be praised”—Palti ben Layish, with David's wife. Why does it not also count this pious man's piety, which is just like Boaz's? Rashi therefore explains that every such pious man is R. Yehudah bar Ilai. Sanhedrin there says “A woman who fears the Lord shall be praised” refers to R. Yehudah bar Ilai, with seven people covering themselves in one cloak and studying Torah, in Heilprin’s wording. The checked Sanhedrin and Zacuto read six students, and the checked Birkat HaZevach reads two. Heilprin also points to Nedarim, chapter 6, where the cloak is shared by Yehudah and his wife. Thus the merit of not approaching the girl is vain beside his other virtue. End of quotation; these are words from a wise mouth that bring favor. He wrapped himself in fringed linen sheets and resembled an angel of the Lord: Shabbat, chapter 2, 25b. He took a myrtle branch and danced before a bride: Ketubot 17a. In HaRoeh, Berakhot 55a, a matron speaks. In the parallel at Nedarim 49b:10 a sectarian speaks. In both, the question is “Your face resembles a lender at interest or pig breeder.” He answered, “Both are forbidden; rather, I have twenty-four privies in which I examine myself.” Jerusalem Talmud, Arvei Pesachim, halakhah 1; Kohelet Midrash, on “Who is like the wise man”; Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of HaMotzi Yayin: she asked whether he was a wine-drinker. He answered, “Learning is with me, as it is written, ‘A man's wisdom lights his face.’” When he drank the four Passover cups, he bound his head until the festival. HaNoder, Nedarim 49b: going to the study house, he carried a pitcher on his shoulder and said, “Great is labor, which honors its owner.” His wife made him a cloak. When he covered himself, he blessed, “Blessed is He who clothed me in a cloak.” Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel decreed a fast, but R. Yehudah did not come. They said he had no covering. He sent him a cloak, but he did not accept it. He lifted the mat and showed wealth beneath it: “Nevertheless, I do not wish to benefit from this world.” This was miraculous. Taanit 30a, near the end: Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name, this was R. Yehudah bar Ilai's practice on the eve of the Ninth of Av: they brought him dry bread with salt; he sat between oven and stove, ate, drank a jug of water, and resembled one whose dead lay before him. Gittin 67a: R. Yehudah is wise when he wishes, which Rashi explains as when he settles his mind. Zacuto adds that his sons died in his lifetime. Tosafot says wise when he wishes, more than R. Meir; perhaps R. Meir was sharp and raised objections, while R. Yehudah was deliberate and reached conclusions. See Rashi there.

(c) He is the authority of an anonymous Sifra, which is Torat Kohanim: the chapter “Rabbi Eliezer of circumcision,” Shabbat 137a, beginning; Yoma 41a, beginning; Eruvin 96b; Kiddushin 53a; Sanhedrin 86a; Shevuot 13a. Tzemach David [הצ״ד; provisional expansion] writes that Rav compiled Sifra according to R. Yehudah bar Ilai's view; see Abba Arikha above.

(d) End of Moed Katan, 21a, and Semachot, chapter 10: when his son died, R. Chananyah ben Akavya was interpreter. R. Chananyah ben Akavya entered and sat beside him. He whispered to R. Chananyah ben Akavya, who whispered to the interpreter, and the interpreter made it heard publicly. R. Yehudah said: an incident with ben Kadera, who wrote forms for bills of divorce in the evening [בערב; time/place reading uncertain]. The sages invalidated all of them; R. Eliezer validates them all except women's bills of divorce: Tosefta Gittin 2:10 (Lieberman). He outlived his colleagues and lived in Rabbi's days; see there. End of Rosh Hashanah, 30b, beginning: we read “R. Yehudah said,” not “R. Yehudah said to him,” for, Heilprin infers, he never saw Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

(e) Gelilot Eretz Yisrael writes that his grave is at Kefar Ein Zetim, north of the village, with a large monument upon it. Nearby are a cave and many monuments; his father R. Ilai and many righteous men are buried there. Elsewhere it writes that R. Yehudah bar Ilai is buried at Kefar Paniam. Joseph's trial concerning Potiphera came in R. Ilai, and this was the reincarnation of R. Yehudah bar Ilai: Emek HaMelekh 75b; Yalkut Reuveni, Vayeshev. See Gilgulim.

(f) R. Yehudah and R. Eliezer ben Yaakov: the law follows R. Eliezer ben Yaakov. R. Meir and R. Yehudah: the law follows R. Yehudah, Eruvin. Tosafot, Berakhot 49b, except where R. Yochanan adopts R. Meir's approach; see Migdal Oz, Eruvin, chapter 1. Sefer Keritot, Yemot Olam, gate 3: the law follows R. Yehudah regarding eruvin, but not partitions. Wherever he taught in Eruvin, the law follows him: end of Chalon. Nevertheless, we hold like the lenient view against him. See Eruvin 46a, 95a; Hagahot Maimoniyyot, Laws of Sabbath, chapter 16; Keneset HaGedolah, Orach Chayyim, section 358. R. Shimon and R. Yehudah: the law follows R. Yehudah—Eruvin there; Bekhorot 11a; Beitzah 27a. It is surprising that Beit Yosef, Yoreh Deah, beginning of section 119, writes the reverse. See Tosafot Yom Tov, Bekhorot 4:9. Chazit Rabbah, on “Sustain me with raisin cakes”: at the end of persecution our teachers assembled at Usha: R. Yehudah, R. Nechemyah, R. Meir, R. Yosi, R. Shimon ben Yochai, R. Elazar son of R. Yosi [the checked Midrash reads Eliezer, son of R. Yosi HaGelili], and R. Eliezer ben Yaakov, etc. They honored R. Yehudah, not because he was greater than they, but because he was a townsman, and a person's place honors him. R. Yehudah entered and expounded.

(g) R. Elazar ben Azaryah was his principal teacher, as in Megillah 20a, beginning, and Berakhot 15b. “R. Yehudah says in R. Elazar ben Azaryah's name”; it says there that he was his teacher. Heilprin calls R. Eliezer his teacher in HaKometz. The passage explains that Yehudah transmitted R. Eliezer’s ruling because Yehudah’s father R. Ilai was R. Eliezer's student; see there. Beitzah 40a: R. Eliezer was R. Yehudah's teacher. Rashba writes: his teacher's teacher. In R. Eliezer's name: Tosefta Nazir, chapter 2. R. Eliezer ben Yaakov said to him. In R. Elazar ben Matya's name. With R. Elazar son of R. Yosi and R. Shimon ben Yochai, he was at Yavneh. R. Elazar, his son; see R. Yosi son of R. Yehudah. Heilprin says he studied before Rabban Gamliel with R. Chananyah ben Akavya and cites Ketubot, chapter 8. Tosefta Ketubot 8:1 records Chananyah relaying Rabban Gamliel’s teaching. Shabbat 103b and Zevachim 79a: in Rabban Gamliel's name; it says there, “This is his own view; that is his teacher's.” R. Chananyah, in his name. R. Yehudah and R. Yosi sent scholars to the son of R. Chanina ben Antigonos. As a minor, he read the scroll before R. Tarfon: Megillah 20a. In R. Tarfon's name: Nazir 34a. Mishnah Nedarim, HaNoder Min HaMevushal: “R. Tarfon forbade it to me.” Sukkah 31a: in R. Tarfon's name. He sat before R. Tarfon: Yevamot 101b. R. Yehudah HaNasi, Rabbi, was his student. Rabbi said, “As a child I read the scroll before R. Yehudah”: Megillah 20a. End of chapter 1 of Shevuot: Rabbi was R. Yehudah's student; see there. R. Yochanan, in his name. R. Yochanan ben Dehavai, in his name. R. Yosi HaGelili, his teacher. In R. Yosi HaGelili's name: Mishnah Bava Kamma, chapter 8, 90a; Makkot 16a and Shevuot 21a. The parallel at Temurah 3a gives the teaching in R. Yosi HaGelili’s name through a chain that omits R. Yehudah. R. Yosi, his son. R. Yishmael son of R. Yosi told him, “My teacher, thus my father explained”: Sukkah 18a. R. Muna, in his name. R. Meyasha, in his name. R. Mani, in R. Yehudah's name, in R. Yosi HaGelili's name: Jerusalem Talmud. R. Nechemyah, his colleague. Sumkhos. R. Yehudah reports that R. Nechunya the well-digger “testified before us”. R. Yehudah was regularly before R. Azaryah: Ruth Midrash and Recanati. Perhaps this is R. Yehudah, and R. Azaryah is R. Elazar's father. R. Azaryah and R. Yehudah son of R. Simon, in R. Yehudah bar Ilai's name. R. Akiva, his teacher. He disagrees with R. Shimon, his colleague. Yuchasin writes: it is surprising that Rambam placed R. Meir, R. Yosi, R. Yehudah, and R. Natan, who was later than R. Shimon ben Yochai, in this group, while putting R. Shimon with Rabbi in the fourth group. This is certainly an obvious error, as appears from the Talmud. See above what I wrote from Chazit Midrash: R. Meir, R. Shimon—R. Shimon ben Yochai—R. Yehudah, and R. Yosi were in one generation. R. Shimon Shezuri, his colleague. R. Shimon son of Rabbi, his student; see above. R. Shimon, his son.
